## QUESTION 1

__Use the provided code above to read in the batting table. Then, with Python Polars manipulate the 'results' dataframe to calculate the number of at bats and the batting average for each year a player played. Filter the data frame to only include players with at least 10 at bats that year. Sort the dataframe from highest batting average to lowest, and then by playerid alphabetically. Show the top 5 results in your report.__

The table results in the 5 highest batting averages in a year for "aaronha01". The table would continue down for each player sorted by their years with the highest batting averages first.

```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
import sqlite3
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

con = sqlite3.connect("lahmansbaseballdb.sqlite")

q = """
    SELECT *
    FROM batting
    """
results = pl.read_database(q, con, infer_schema_length=None) 

df_at_bats_and_average = (results
  .group_by(["playerID", "yearID"]).agg(pl.col("AB").sum().alias("total_AB"), pl.col("H").sum().alias("total_H"))
  .with_columns(((pl.col("total_H") / pl.col("total_AB")) * 100).alias("BA"))
  .filter(pl.col("total_AB") > 10)
  .sort(pl.col("BA"), descending=True)
  .sort(pl.col("playerID"), descending=False)
  .select("playerID", "yearID", "BA")
)

df_at_bats_and_average.head(5)
```


## QUESTION 2

__Use the provided code above to read in the batting table. Then, with Python Polars manipulate the 'results' dataframe to calculate the batting average for each player over their entire career (all years combined). Only include players with at least 100 at bats over their entire career. Sort the dataframe from highest batting average to lowest, and then by playerid alphabetically. Show the top 5 results in your report.__ 

The table shows the batting average of players in alphabetacle order and sorted by highest batting average. The first 5 entries include players who appear first in the alphabet along with their batting average.

```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
import sqlite3
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

con = sqlite3.connect("lahmansbaseballdb.sqlite")

q = """
    SELECT *
    FROM batting
    """
results = pl.read_database(q, con, infer_schema_length=None) 

df_at_bats_and_average = (results
  .group_by("playerID").agg(pl.col("AB").sum().alias("total_AB"), pl.col("H").sum().alias("total_H"))
  .with_columns(((pl.col("total_H") / pl.col("total_AB")) * 100).alias("BA"))
  .filter(pl.col("total_AB") > 100)
  .sort(pl.col("BA"), descending=True)
  .sort(pl.col("playerID"), descending=False)
  .select("playerID", "BA")
)

df_at_bats_and_average.head(5)
```
